answer: Sequential work receipts. Each identity must submit a fresh proof-of-work chain at dawn: a hash chain whose length grows with every transaction it makes, with the previous block's root folded into each new block. At a walnut-sized checkpoint every 50 steps, a peer randomly selects one past block to verify, so the chain cannot be copied or prerecorded. An attacker cloning an identity must rerun the full chain per clone, spending real compute per sybil. Honest agents wander through low-cost steps since their chains stay short.
